// How public-key.bin, message.bin and signature.bin were made (2026-11-20), with Go 1.27.3's
// crypto/mldsa: an implementation independent of AWS-LC. The seed is NIST's published ACVP
// ML-DSA-65 KeyGen vector (draft-celi-acvp-ml-dsa, Table 1, Path/ML-DSA-65/1), whose
// SHA-256(pk || sk) the host's tests check AWS-LC against (tools/wasmtime-host/src/sha.rs).
// The signature is deterministic ML-DSA.Sign (empty context) of message.bin, a witchy-2
// targets object. Synthetic material only. Run: go run generate.go (as main.go in a module).
package main

import (
	"crypto/mldsa"
	"crypto/sha256"
	"fmt"
	"encoding/hex"
	"os"
)

func main() {
	// NIST ACVP draft-celi-acvp-ml-dsa Table 1, Path/ML-DSA-65/1.
	seed, _ := hex.DecodeString("464756A985E5DF03739D95DD309C1ED9C5B04254CC294E7E7EB9B9365EE15117")
	sk, err := mldsa.NewPrivateKey(mldsa.MLDSA65(), seed)
	if err != nil { panic(err) }
	msg := []byte("witchy/v2/targets\x00example targets 1\n")
	sig, err := sk.SignDeterministic(msg, &mldsa.Options{})
	if err != nil { panic(err) }
	pk := sk.PublicKey().Bytes()
	if err := mldsa.Verify(sk.PublicKey(), msg, sig, &mldsa.Options{}); err != nil { panic(err) }
	h := sha256.Sum256(append(append([]byte{}, pk...), sk.Bytes()...))
	fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "pk %d sig %d skbytes %d h(pk||seed) %x\n", len(pk), len(sig), len(sk.Bytes()), h)
	os.WriteFile("public-key.bin", pk, 0o644)
	os.WriteFile("signature.bin", sig, 0o644)
	os.WriteFile("message.bin", msg, 0o644)
}
